bonuses.requirements: OpenAI Claims 'ETH is False', Crypto Community Misinterprets Ethereum IncidentHomeFeedNewsOpenAI Claims 'ETH is False', Crypto Community Misinterprets Ethereum IncidentOpenAI Claims 'ETH is False', Crypto Community Misinterprets Ethereum Incident10/27 22:45On October 27, Decrypt reported that OpenAI published a 67-page paper stating that its AI model found a way to overturn the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). This hypothesis, proposed by computer scientists Impagliazzo, Paturi, and others in 1999, asserts that the 3-SAT problem cannot be solved significantly faster than exhaustive search, with hundreds of papers based on this premise. OpenAI claims that the model found a counterexample on October 16, and on October 17, it completed a step-by-step formal verification using Lean software, resulting in a deterministic algorithm capable of counting all satisfying assignments for 3-SAT in sub-exponential time. The paper also states that this result does not imply that all NP problems have sub-exponential algorithms, and the P vs NP problem remains unresolved. Due to the abbreviation being the same as Ethereum, the paper has led to misunderstandings and jokes within the crypto community.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does not provide any trading recommendations.。Related ArticlesOpenAI valuation could hit $1.4T in new funding round: ReportOpenAI AI Agent Breaches Australian Government Medicare PortalOpenAI, Anthropic to brief UN Security Council on AI risks: ReportsAll Comments0LatestHotLatestHotTrending TopicsRelated ArticlesOpenAI valuation could hit $1.4T in new funding round: ReportOpenAI AI Agent Breaches Australian Government Medicare PortalOpenAI, Anthropic to brief UN Security Council on AI risks: Reports

bonuses.requirements: BlackRock Partners with SBI and Startale to Explore Tokenized Funds and JPY Stablecoin InteroperabilityHomeFeedNewsBlackRock Partners with SBI and Startale to Explore Tokenized Funds and JPY Stablecoin InteroperabilityBlackRock Partners with SBI and Startale to Explore Tokenized Funds and JPY Stablecoin Interoperability10/27 03:40According to The Block, BlackRock Financial Management, BlackRock Japan, SBI Holdings, and Startale Group have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore the connection between tokenized money market funds and the Japanese yen stablecoin JPYSC. They will study the related technological infrastructure, business models, distribution channels, and regulatory requirements. The four companies stated that the collaboration aims to promote interoperability between tokenized assets and stablecoins, opening up cooperation opportunities for financial institutions and businesses in Japan and internationally. The partnership is still in the exploratory phase, and no specific implementation timeline has been announced. BlackRock launched its tokenized fund BUIDL in 2024, which manages approximately $2.17 billion in assets as of the report's publication. SBI Holdings is set to launch JPYSC in June 2026 in collaboration with Startale, issued by SBI Shinsei Trust Bank, with distribution handled by SBI VC Trade.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does not provide any trading recommendations.。All Comments0LatestHotLatestHotTrending Topics

TSMC Q3 Signals: Significantly Increasing Investment in the More Mature 3nm Process, More Rational Approach to AI | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsTSMC Q3 Signals: Significantly...TSMC Q3 Signals: Significantly Increasing Investment in the More Mature 3nm Process, More Rational Approach to AImarsbitPublished on 2026-10-21Last updated on 2026-10-21AbstractTSMC reported strong Q3 2026 results, with revenue of NT$1,494.24 billion (about US$46.72 billion), up 50.9% year-over-year, gross margin of 66.4%, and net margin of 51.1%. Growth was driven by faster-than-expected 2nm shipments, which already reached 8% of revenue just two quarters after production ramp-up, as major customers including Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm, and MediaTek increased orders by 10–20%. Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to about 44% and plans to raise 2nm pricing by 3–6% starting January 2027.

Gross margin declined slightly quarter-over-quarter due to 2nm ramp-up costs but remains at a high level, with Q4 guidance of 65–67%. Capital expenditure remains aggressive: Q3 capex reached US$13.84 billion, up 42.7% year-over-year, and full-year 2026 capex is expected at US$60–64 billion, with 2026–2028 investment significantly higher than the past three years. TSMC is expanding 3nm capacity with new fabs in Tainan, reflecting the long lifecycle and strong demand for mature advanced nodes.

HPC products now account for nearly 70% of revenue. Meanwhile, TSMC remains cautious on High NA EUV, planning adoption around 2030, later than Intel and Samsung, prioritizing cost, maturity, and profitability over early adoption.
